segments.say: On January 1st, 2027, California bans food with Red No. 3. There's no sell-through period.
segments.beat: One night to clear the shelves

segments.say: The dye hides under many names: erythrosine, E127, "Red 3", even scanning typos. It's in hundreds of products, on thousands of shelf spots, and stores get one overnight shift to clear it.

Miss one, and it's a violation. Pull the wrong one, since Red 40 looks almost the same on a label, and you empty shelves for nothing. Our simulated drill is for a large big-box retailer with nearly 300 California stores.
Gemini 4 Argon wrote this working system this morning, in one generation. Here it runs on 20 of those stores, overnight.
segments.beat: A working system, written this morning

segments.say: Inside a store, flashing tags are pulls still to do. Associates walk to each shelf, pull the product, and put a substitute in its place.
Every decision shows its evidence: erythrosine found, a vague "artificial color" held for a person, a Red 40 look-alike left on the shelf.
It found all 467 products with Red No. 3, pulled 0 of the 483 look-alikes, and covered all 6,718 shelf spots, with 0 plan mistakes. 1 extra item was pulled, one our rules say to check by hand.
Argon's first draft missed 25 of the 467, leaving 350 shelf spots with banned product. Three small logged fixes closed the gap.
Simulated drill, simulated operations, every number from the verifier.
